decision.reason: The position is still in range and drift does not justify paying gas, realising impermanent loss, and resetting fee accrual.

limitations: A single frozen block describes one moment and does not predict the next one.
Oracle mean ticks describe what happened, not what will happen.

execution.reason: Canned Range Keeper v1 observes and recommends. It never removes liquidity, mints liquidity, swaps, or approves spending.

marketContext.note: Drift is the current tick minus the pool's own arithmetic-mean tick over each window. Tick direction is quote-dependent: a rising tick is a rising token1-per-token0 price and a falling token0-per-token1 price. It is a description of what happened, not a forecast.

relativeToRange.note: Movement measured against this position's own range width, so it reads the same in either price quote convention.

rangeStatus.composition: Mixed token0 and token1; the split moves toward token0 as price falls and toward token1 as price rises.

costOfActing: gas for decrease, collect, and mint
realised impermanent loss at the current price
slippage if the position is rebalanced through a swap
costOfNotActing: the position may leave the range and stop earning fees
a later rebalance may happen at a worse price
tradeoffs.note: Constant rebalancing is not automatically better. Holding is the correct answer whenever expected fees do not cover the cost of acting.
